{"id":"069ff508-eb39-487b-adad-35a75802277e","object":"chat.completion","created":1790475945,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{
  "target": "the identity of the Europa Universalis IV downloadable content that made religion and technology changes and added new mechanics for a European nation",
  "subject": {
    "description": "the specific Europa Universalis IV downloadable content in question",
    "status": "unresolved_referent",
    "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
  },
  "required_background": [
    {
      "statement": "The strategy video game referred to in the Original Question is Europa Universalis IV.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "A downloadable content pack was released for Europa Universalis IV more than three years after its release.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "The downloadable content in question made changes to the base game's religion and technology mechanics.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "The downloadable content in question added new mechanics for a specific playable European nation.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q"]
    }
  ],
  "decision": "discover_subject"
}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need analyze candidate need. Need determine target, subject, required background, decision.

We have Original Question. Verified Claims C1 C2. Working Hypothesis says game is EU4 but cannot use as support. Candidate Need: "Which Europa Universalis IV downloadable content made changes to the base game's religion and technology mechanics and added new mechanics for a specific playable European nation?"

We need separate target: identify DLC matching description? Target: the DLC (or which DLC) that made changes to religion/technology and new mechanics for European nation. Subject: Europa Universalis IV downloadable content? Is subject grounded? Original Question describes a pack of DLC for a strategy video game over three years after release; Master's thesis on postcolonialism in this game etc. Verified Claims establish thesis on Europa Universalis IV at Georgetown, advisor Amanda Phillips. They do not explicitly establish that game is EU4? C1 says thesis title "Is EU4 Only About Map Painting?" Settler Colonial Ideology in Europa Universalis IV. So Original Question refers to "this game" in thesis. C1 identifies thesis about Europa Universalis IV. Thus EU4 is grounded? Subject is EU4 DLC. But Candidate Need refers to "Europa Universalis IV downloadable content" and asks which DLC with features. Is that subject already identifiable? The DLC itself not identified. But subject of candidate need is "which EU4 DLC" (unresolved referent) because DLC not identified. However, "Europa Universalis IV" is grounded from C1. The DLC that matches description is the target. The concrete subject? It asks about an entity (DLC) to be discovered. Hmm.

Need determine required background facts. For Candidate Need to ask "Which EU4 DLC made changes..." it presupposes:
- There exists a DLC for EU4 that made changes to religion and technology mechanics and new mechanics for a specific playable European nation. Is this supported? Original Question states: "The downloadable content in question made changes to the mechanics of the base game including religion and technology, and new mechanics for a specific playable European nation." That is Q. So supported by Q. Also "The strategy video game is EU4" maybe supported by C1? C1 says thesis on EU4, and Original Question says thesis on this game. Need connection: C1 states thesis on EU4, Q says "A Master's thesis was written on the theme of postcolonialism in this game for an American University in 2023..." It doesn't name game. C1 identifies thesis and game. So Q + C1 establishes game is EU4? C1 says thesis on EU4. Q says thesis on this game. So yes, by linking Q's "this game" to C1's EU4? Need be careful: Q has multiple references: "this game" in sentence "A Master's thesis was written on the theme of postcolonialism in this game..." refers to strategy video game. C1 states 2023 thesis on EU4. So strategy game = EU4. Supported by Q and C1. But Candidate Need subject is EU4 DLC; game grounded. DLC not identified; identifying it is target. The required background: There was a DLC released for EU4 over three years after its release? Q says "A pack of downloadable content was released for a strategy video game over three years after its release." If strategy game = EU4, that's supported by Q + C1. The DLC made changes to religion and technology and new mechanics for European nation is supported by Q. The specific playable European nation? Q says specific, not named. That can be part of target or maybe background? Candidate Need says "specific playable European nation" not named, so it's a variable. The DLC's features are part of the description to identify it. Actually Candidate Need asks "Which EU4 DLC made changes..." The target is identity of DLC. Required background: There exists some DLC for EU4 with those changes? Q states the DLC in question made those changes. So yes. But to ask "which" we need that DLC is not identified? That's fine, target unresolved. Subject? The subject could be "the EU4 DLC that made religion/tech changes and new mechanics for a European nation" — this is a description, not yet a concrete entity. Status maybe unresolved_referent because no DLC ID. But the Candidate Need is discovering that subject. According to decision categories: "discover_subject" when Candidate Need requires a concrete entity/source/event that has not yet been identified. Here the DLC itself is not identified; but the Candidate Need is exactly asking to identify it. Should decision be "keep" or "discover_subject"? The instruction: "Do not reject a question merely because its TARGET is unresolved." If target is identity of DLC, subject is the DLC? Wait need parse.

Candidate Need: "Which Europa Universalis IV downloadable content made changes to the base game's religion and technology mechanics and added new mechanics for a specific playable European nation?" This is a question to identify DLC. The TARGET is the identity of that DLC. The SUBJECT is the DLC? But if subject is the DLC, not yet identified. However, the question itself seeks to identify it. The schema distinguishes TARGET and SUBJECT. TARGET: what relation/attribute is Candidate Need asking to discover. SUBJECT: concrete entity/source/event/object Candidate Need is asking about. Determine whether subject already identifiable. In "Which entity matches description D?" the instructions say identifying the entity is the TARGET. So subject may be description D? Hmm. Example: "Which entity matches description D?" → identifying the entity is the TARGET. So subject might be the set/description? They don't provide subject example. But decision "discover_subject" when Candidate Need requires a concrete entity/source/event that has not yet been identified. That seems exactly this: the DLC is not identified. But if we treat identifying the entity as TARGET, then subject could be the description? Need decide.

The Candidate Need is not asking "Does the identified DLC have property P?" It's asking "Which DLC has properties?" That is a discovery request for a concrete DLC. The target is the DLC identity. The subject is the DLC (unresolved). Decision should likely be "discover_subject" because concrete DLC not yet identified. However, the Original Question itself already asks for content designer of this DLC. Candidate Need is a sub-question to identify DLC. The DLC is not named in Q or claims. So yes, subject unresolved_referent. The goal is to discover subject. So "discover_subject".

But let's carefully evaluate required background. Need list facts must be true for Candidate Need to ask its TARGET in this form. Candidate Need presupposes:
1. Europa Universalis IV is a strategy video game? Is that needed? The Candidate Need specifically names EU4. Is EU4 established? C1 mentions thesis on EU4. But does it establish EU4 is a strategy video game? Original Question says strategy video game; C1 says thesis on EU4. It doesn't explicitly state EU4 is a strategy video game, but likely. "Do not use outside knowledge." C1 only mentions game title. Original Question says strategy video game. To link, need thesis was on this game. C1 says thesis on EU4; Q says thesis on this game. So EU4 = this game = strategy video game? Q says "for a strategy video game" and "this game" in thesis. So yes, if thesis is on this game, and C1 says thesis on EU4, then EU4 is the strategy video game. But the claim doesn't state EU4 is a video game? It says thesis about Europa Universalis IV. The title includes EU4. It's a game? The thesis title "Is EU4 Only About Map Painting? Settler Colonial Ideology in Europa Universalis IV" implies EU4 is a game? Not necessarily explicitly "video game", but combined with Q, yes. Might be okay. But required background can include "The strategy video game in the Original Question is Europa Universalis IV." Status supported by Q+C1? Q says thesis on this game; C1 says thesis on EU4. But Q also says "for a strategy video game over three years after its release. A Master's thesis was written ... in this game..." The "this game" refers to strategy video game. So yes.

2. A downloadable content pack was released for that game over three years after its release. Q states this. Support Q (and C1 for game).
3. The DLC made changes to base game mechanics including religion and technology. Q states.
4. The DLC introduced new mechanics for a specific playable European nation. Q states.

Maybe also "The DLC is a Europa Universalis IV downloadable content" — supported by Q+C1 if game EU4.

The Candidate Need asks "Which EU4 DLC made changes..." It doesn't require that DLC has already been identified. It requires the features to identify it. So required background includes those features. They are supported by Q. So if subject were grounded? The subject of the Candidate Need is the DLC. It is not identified. The question's purpose is to identify it. Thus subject status unresolved_referent. Decision discover_subject.

Alternatively, if we consider the subject as "Europa Universalis IV downloadable content" (the class), that is grounded via Q+C1. The target is which specific DLC. Then decision keep? Because subject adequately grounded and required background supported. The instructions: "Use 'discover_subject' when the Candidate Need requires a concrete entity/source/event that has not yet been identified." Here it requires a concrete DLC that has not yet been identified. So discover_subject. Also "Use 'keep' when the subject is adequately grounded and every required background fact is supported." The subject "Europa Universalis IV downloadable content" as a class is grounded, but the specific DLC is not. The question is asking which DLC. The target is not the DLC identity? Let's map: TARGET: relation/attribute asking to discover. The Candidate Need asks to discover the identity of the DLC. So target could be "the identity of the EU4 DLC matching description". Subject: the DLC? If subject is unresolved, discover_subject. But the examples: "Which entity matches description D?" → identifying the entity is the TARGET. That suggests the target is the identity. What is subject? Maybe the description D? If identifying entity is target, then subject might be the description or the set of entities. But then subject can be grounded (the description exists). Hmm.

Let's read prompt carefully:

"Your task is to separate:
1. TARGET: What relation or attribute is the Candidate Need actually asking us to discover? The TARGET is allowed to be unresolved.
2. SUBJECT: What concrete entity, source, event, relationship, or object is the Candidate Need asking about? Determine whether that subject is already identifiable from the Original Question or Verified Claims.
3. REQUIRED BACKGROUND: What facts must already be true for the Candidate Need to ask its TARGET in this form? These are background presuppositions, not the TARGET itself."

Example:
"Did X perform event R?"
→ R is the TARGET. It may be unresolved.
"What year did X perform event R?"
→ X performed R is REQUIRED BACKGROUND. If that event has not been established, the question is premature.

"Which entity matches description D?"
→ identifying the entity is the TARGET.

"Does the entity described by D have property P?"
→ if no concrete entity has yet been identified and checking P requires such a binding, the subject may still be unresolved.

So for "Which entity matches D?", target = identifying entity. Subject? The subject is perhaps "entity described by D" but no concrete entity identified. They don't state decision for this, but likely "discover_subject" if no entity identified? Actually the example says identifying entity is TARGET. That implies the Candidate Need is allowed; the TARGET is unresolved. But then subject? It might be unresolved_referent because the entity isn't identified. But if the goal is to identify the entity, decision might be "discover_subject". The example "Does the entity described by D have property P?" says if no concrete entity identified, subject may still be unresolved. That is different: asking property P of an entity that hasn't been identified is premature; you should first discover subject. But "Which entity matches D?" is not premature; it's a discovery question. So decision for "Which entity matches D?" could be "discover_subject" (because it's asking to discover subject) or "keep" (because it's a valid discovery target). The decision options: "keep" when subject adequately grounded and every required background supported. "discover_subject" when Candidate Need requires a concrete entity/source/event that has not yet been identified. So "Which entity matches D?" requires a concrete entity not yet identified, so "discover_subject". That seems right.

Our Candidate Need: "Which EU4 DLC made changes...?" It requires a concrete DLC not yet identified. So decision = discover_subject.

Now, subject description: "the specific Europa Universalis IV downloadable content that made religion/technology changes and added mechanics for a European nation" or simply "the Europa Universalis IV downloadable content in question". Status: unresolved_referent. basis_refs: Q, C1? Because Q mentions DLC, C1 identifies game. But the DLC itself not identified. We can say basis_refs: ["Q", "C1"] because grounded as EU4 DLC? Actually unresolved referent, basis refs indicate what grounds the subject? The schema says basis_refs for subject. If unresolved, basis_refs can list what establishes the existence/context? Probably Q and C1. But if subject is the specific DLC, no claim identifies it, so basis_refs might be empty? Hmm. The subject is "the EU4 DLC matching description". Is that identifiable? It is described in Q but not identified. The description exists in Q. The game is from C1. So basis_refs Q, C1. Status "unresolved_referent" because no concrete entity identified. That seems fine.

Required background:
- "The strategy video game in the Original Question is Europa Universalis IV." Supported by Q + C1. Is it required? Candidate Need names EU4. For it to be the right game, yes. It is supported.
- "A downloadable content pack was released for Europa Universalis IV over three years after its release." Supported by Q + C1? Q says released for strategy video game over three years after release; C1 links game. Yes.
- "The downloadable content in question made changes to the base game's religion and technology mechanics." Supported by Q.
- "The downloadable content in question added new mechanics for a specific playable European nation." Supported by Q.
Maybe also "The DLC is for EU4" included in second.
- "Europa Universalis IV is a strategy video game." Is this required? Candidate Need doesn't need this to ask which DLC made changes, only that EU4 has DLC. But Q identifies strategy game as EU4. It might be background. But Candidate Need specifically says "Europa Universalis IV downloadable content", presupposes EU4 exists. That's trivial. We can include if needed. But keep concise.

Need decision. Let's consider if any required background is unsupported. All supported by Q? The link to EU4 is via C1. Q says thesis on this game, C1 says thesis on EU4. So yes. But is "The strategy video game is EU4" explicitly supported? C1 says thesis on EU4, Q says thesis on this game. Yes.

However, note C1 says "The 2023 master's thesis ... was written by Mitchell Losito at Georgetown University." It doesn't explicitly say it was on the strategy video game? Q says "A Master's thesis was written on the theme of postcolonialism in this game..." C1's title includes "Europa Universalis IV". So yes, thesis is on EU4. The game in Q is the game the thesis is on. Therefore EU4 is the game. Good.

The Candidate Need asks "Which EU4 DLC made changes..." The required background that DLC made changes to religion and technology and new mechanics for European nation is exactly the description. It is supported by Q. But wait, Q says "The downloadable content in question made changes..." That presupposes there is a specific DLC. It doesn't name it. So the Candidate Need is asking to identify it. The subject is not identified. So discover_subject.

What about the "specific playable European nation" — the Candidate Need says "a specific playable European nation" but doesn't name it. Is the existence of a specific European nation supported? Q says "new mechanics for a specific playable European nation." So yes. But the identity of that nation is not needed for Candidate Need? It might be part of target? Actually target is DLC identity. The nation is part of description. Could be a required background: there is a specific playable European nation for which the DLC added new mechanics. Supported by Q. But it's not a separate fact? We can include.

Now output JSON. Need short natural language. Ensure valid JSON.

Let's draft:

{
  "target": "the identity of the Europa Universalis IV downloadable content that made religion and technology changes and added new mechanics for a European nation",
  "subject": {
    "description": "the specific Europa Universalis IV downloadable content in question",
    "status": "unresolved_referent",
    "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
  },
  "required_background": [
    {
      "statement": "The strategy video game referred to in the Original Question is Europa Universalis IV.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "A downloadable content pack was released for Europa Universalis IV more than three years after its release.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q", "C1"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "The downloadable content in question made changes to the base game's religion and technology mechanics.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q"]
    },
    {
      "statement": "The downloadable content in question added new mechanics for a specific playable European nation.",
      "status": "supported",
      "basis_refs": ["Q"]
    }
  ],
  "decision": "discover_subject"
}

Check if any unsupported? The link "Q + C1" for game: Q says thesis on this game; C1 says thesis on EU4. Yes. But Q also says "A pack of downloadable content was released for a strategy video game over three years after its release." The DLC is for the strategy game. So if game is EU4, DLC for EU4. supported.

Should we include "Europa Universalis IV is a strategy video game" as required? Maybe not necessary. But Candidate Need names EU4; to be the same game, yes. We already have first.

Subject basis_refs: if unresolved, basis_refs maybe Q and C1 because the description comes from Q and game from C1. That's okay. Alternatively empty because no concrete subject. But schema expects basis_refs. We'll include Q, C1.

Decision: discover_subject. Is there any possibility "lift_premise"? The Candidate Need asks downstream attribute (which DLC) of relation/event that is unsupported? The relation/event is "DLC made changes..." is supported by Q. The DLC identity itself is unsupported. That's discover subject, not lift premise. "lift_premise" would be if asking e.g. "What year did DLC X release?" before DLC X is identified. Here asking to identify DLC. So discover_subject.

One nuance: Original Question ultimately asks "What was the full name of the third content designer credited for this downloadable content?" The DLC must be identified. Candidate Need is a sub-question. It is asking to identify DLC. So yes.

Need output only JSON.
